seoTitle: Crown Rips Review 2026: Free Packs & Buyback
metaDescription: Crown Rips gives a free pack on signup, three more each week, and buys cards back at 100% into a withdrawable balance. Our review of the daily and terms.

sections.heading: What Crown Rips actually is
body: Crown Rips is a digital pack-opening app covering Pokemon and sports cards. You buy a pack, the app rips it on screen, and a real card lands in your account. From there you have three choices: have it shipped to you, leave it in the vault, or sell it back to Crown Rips for its market value.

That last option is the one that matters, and it is where Crown Rips separates itself from most of the field. The buyback credits a cash balance you can withdraw, rather than store credit that can only ever buy more packs. On a lot of these sites the money technically never leaves the building. Here it can.

Packs start at $1 for the Entry tier and run up to $3,000 for Mythic, with the top advertised pull somewhere around $100,000. It is available everywhere in the US except Nevada, and the minimum age is 19 rather than the 18 the rest of this category settles on, which catches people out.

sections.heading: The free pack, and why it is the only guaranteed value here
body: New accounts get a free $1 welcome pack after signup and email verification. No promo code is needed and no deposit is required, which makes it the cheapest way to test whether the whole pipeline works for you.

We would treat that free pack, and the daily rewards below, as the entire reason to open an account. Buying packs is not a good deal and we are not going to pretend otherwise. The expected value of a pack sits below what you pay for it, because that gap is how the business makes money. No buyback rate changes that arithmetic, and a 100% buyback does not mean you break even. It means you get back the operator's valuation of whatever you happened to pull, which on most rips is worth considerably less than the pack cost.
Free packs are the exception, because there is no purchase to be underwater on. Rip the free pack, sell it back, and whatever it was worth is yours.

sections.heading: Read the 100% buyback carefully
body: Crown Rips advertises a 100% fair-market-value buyback, which is the best rate available in this category alongside Rips by Triumph. Two things are worth understanding about what that number actually promises.

First, it is 100% of the operator's own valuation of the card you pulled. It is not 100% of what you paid for the pack, and the two are rarely close. If you buy a $30 pack and pull a card Crown Rips values at $4, a 100% buyback pays you $4.

Second, and more positively, it pays into a withdrawable cash balance rather than site credit. Most of this category does the same, but not all of it: Packz pays its 90% in store credit that can only buy more packs, and Courtside converts cards to coins instead. Check which you are getting before you judge a percentage.

One condition to know going in: cash you deposit has to be played through before you can withdraw it, and identity verification is required before any withdrawal clears. Get the verification done on the day you sign up rather than the day you first try to cash out.

sections.heading: The three-day vault clock
body: This is the trap on Crown Rips, and it is worth setting a reminder for. Cards left sitting in the vault are sold back automatically after three days.

That is the shortest window of any site on our list. Rips by Triumph gives you seven days to decide, and Tilt Rips runs a notably longer claim window than most. Three days means that if you pull something you actually wanted to keep and then do not open the app over a weekend, the decision gets made for you and the card is gone.
If you are ripping for cards rather than for cash, treat shipping as something you action immediately rather than think about later.

sections.heading: How to test it without risking anything
body: The useful thing about a free signup pack and a withdrawable balance is that together they let you test the entire pipeline for nothing, which is exactly what we would do before depositing on any site in this category.

Sign up, complete identity verification straight away, claim the free $1 pack, rip it, and sell the card back. That puts a small real balance in your account. Then withdraw it. If the withdrawal clears cleanly, you have confirmed the part that actually matters, at zero cost. If it does not, you have learned that for the price of nothing, which is a far better outcome than discovering it with $200 in there.
Run the same test on any rip site before you put money in. On Crown Rips it is unusually easy because the free pack arrives before any purchase.

sections.heading: Who it suits
body: Crown Rips makes most sense if you are here for the free value and happy to treat the packs themselves as entertainment rather than investment. The free signup pack, three free packs a week from the daily, and the milestone drops add up to a reasonable return for a daily login, and the cash balance means that return is real money rather than credit toward more packs.

It suits you less if you want to collect. The three-day vault clock works against anyone who wants to think about whether to ship, and the shipping decision has to be made faster here than anywhere else we cover.

faqs.q: Is the Crown Rips welcome pack really free?
faqs.a: Yes. New accounts get a free $1 pack after signup and email verification, with no promo code and no deposit required. It is the cheapest way to test whether the whole pipeline works before you put money in.

faqs.q: Does Crown Rips pay out in cash?
faqs.a: Yes. The 100% buyback credits a cash balance you can withdraw, rather than store credit that can only buy more packs. Six of the eight sites we track now pay out this way; Packz pays in site credit and Courtside converts cards to coins.

faqs.q: Does a 100% buyback mean I break even on a pack?
faqs.a: No, and this trips a lot of people up. It is 100% of the operator’s valuation of the card you pulled, not 100% of what the pack cost. Pull a $4 card from a $30 pack and the buyback pays $4.

faqs.q: What happens to cards I leave in the Crown Rips vault?
faqs.a: They are sold back automatically after three days, which is the shortest window of any site we track. If you want a card shipped, action it straight away rather than leaving it to decide later.

faqs.q: What is the Crown Rips daily bonus worth?
faqs.a: Across a week it pays $0.70 in cash and three free packs, with packs on days 2, 5 and 7. There are also milestone gifts at days 8, 15, 22 and 30 paying $0.50, $1, $1.50 and $2. No purchase is needed for any of it.

faqs.q: How old do you have to be to use Crown Rips, and where is it available?
faqs.a: 19, which is a year older than every other card rip site on our list, and it is available across the US except Nevada. Some write-ups add Idaho, Louisiana, Michigan, Montana, Washington, Connecticut and New Jersey to that list, but those are Crown Coins sweepstakes casino restrictions and Crown Coins is a different operator.

eligibility.note: Crown Rips is available across the United States except Nevada, and the minimum age is 19 rather than the 18 every other site in this category sets. That is worth knowing if you are 18: this is the one place on the list you cannot use yet. The terms carry no prominent state eligibility section, which is why several third-party lists get the states wrong, claiming Crown Rips also bars Idaho, Louisiana, Michigan, Montana, Washington, Connecticut and New Jersey. Those are Crown Coins sweepstakes casino restrictions, a different operator, and they do not apply here.

seoTitle: Tilt Rips Review 2026: A Free Pack Every Day
metaDescription: Tilt Rips hands you a free pack every day with no purchase, and packs improve as your streak runs. Our review of the daily and the 90% buyback.

sections.heading: A free pack a day, and no catch we could find
body: Most sites in this category call something a daily reward and then attach a condition to it. Tilt Rips does not. Open the app, tap the day, take a pack. No purchase, no deposit, no minimum spend sitting quietly in the terms.

That alone makes it the best free daily we have found in card rips, and it is not especially close. Crown Rips gives three packs a week. Pullz makes you collect seven stamps before a pack appears. Rips by Triumph puts a padlock on all three of its recurring rewards until you buy something. Tilt Rips just hands you one, every day, from day one.

The streak also upgrades as it runs. The standard gold pack covers roughly the first twenty-four days, then the grid switches to a better red tier from day twenty-five and keeps running past day thirty. There is a daily mini game sitting alongside it as well.

A word on the $100,000 maximum pull plastered across the top of that screen: that is a ceiling on what the pack pool contains, not a figure you should have in your head. The realistic outcome of a free daily pack is a card worth a dollar or two. The point is not the ceiling, it is that you are getting one every day for nothing.

sections.heading: Where Tilt Rips gets it right: you can see what you are buying
body: Odds are published before you open anything, and the app shows live market values on pulls rather than a number it made up. For a category this young and this lightly regulated, that is worth more than it sounds. Two of the eight sites we track publish no odds at all.

Shipping fees are also shown before you confirm, which is not universal either. Several operators let you get all the way to a decision before telling you what posting a four-dollar card is going to cost.
The vault window is generous too. Where Crown Rips sells your card back automatically after three days, Tilt Rips gives you a notably longer run at deciding what to do with it.

sections.heading: And where it falls down: shipping takes weeks
body: Delivery can take up to six weeks. That is the longest wait on our list by a wide margin and it is the main reason Tilt Rips does not rank higher.

In practice it matters less than it reads, because most people on these apps are selling back rather than shipping. If you are treating the daily as a small cash stream, you will never touch the post. But if you pull something you genuinely want in your hands, you are waiting a month and a half for it.
The buyback is 90% of market value rather than the 100% Crown Rips and Triumph advertise. On a free pack that distinction barely registers. On a balance you built by spending, it does.

On the buyback itself, the wallet is withdrawable in USD or crypto, and Tilt Rips charges no fees beyond what the app displays before you confirm. Valuations come from live market data and are not open to dispute, which cuts both ways: you will not get a negotiated price, but you are also not at the mercy of someone's opinion of your card.

sections.heading: What the user reviews actually say
body: Tilt Rips sits around 3.6 on the App Store across more than four hundred reviews. We read through them rather than quoting the number and leaving it there.

The praise is consistent: people like the app design and the quality of what they pull. The complaints cluster into three piles, and they are the same three every time. Support is slow. Shipping costs more than expected. And a recurring theme of people describing it as a gambling app wearing a collector's jacket, which is a fair thing to sit with before you deposit.

The operator is Tilt Rips LLC, a Nevada company, and the app launched in May 2026. That is a short track record, so treat it accordingly: test a withdrawal before you build a balance worth caring about.

sections.heading: The honest way to play this one
body: Claim the daily, sell the pack back, and let a balance accumulate slowly for nothing. Do not buy packs expecting to come out ahead, because the maths does not support that on any site in this category and Tilt Rips is no exception.

If the streak is the whole reason you are here, and we think it should be, then the thing to protect is the streak itself. The pack tier improves at day twenty-five, so the back half of a month is worth more than the front half. Set a reminder and keep the chain going.

faqs.q: Is the Tilt Rips daily pack really free?
faqs.a: Yes. There is no purchase or deposit required to claim it, unlike Rips by Triumph where the recurring rewards stay locked until you buy a pack. Log in, tap the day, take the pack.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss a day on the Tilt Rips streak?
faqs.a: The streak is what upgrades your pack tier, with the better red packs starting around day 25, so breaking it costs you the improved packs rather than just one day's claim. Keep the chain going if the streak is why you are there.

faqs.q: How long does Tilt Rips take to ship a card?
faqs.a: Up to six weeks, which is the longest wait of any card rip site we track. Fees are shown before you confirm. If you want the card in your hands quickly, this is the wrong site for it.

faqs.q: What is the Tilt Rips buyback rate?
faqs.a: 90% of market value, credited instantly to your Tilt Rips wallet and withdrawable in USD or several cryptocurrencies, with no fees beyond what the app shows. Crown Rips, CrownCards, Rips by Triumph and PrizePicks all pay 100%, so this is the lowest cash rate among the sites we recommend.

faqs.q: Is Tilt Rips legit?
faqs.a: It is a real operator, Tilt Rips LLC of Nevada, running since May 2026 with published odds and live market values. The app rates around 3.6 on the App Store, with complaints focused on support speed and shipping costs rather than on non-payment. As with any newer site, test a small withdrawal before building a balance.

eligibility.note: The Tilt Rips collectibles terms restrict access by country rather than by state, and name no US state at all. Shipping carries a quantity cap of three graded and three raw cards rather than any geographic limit. The operator is Tilt Rips LLC, a Nevada company, which does not by itself bar Nevada residents.

metaDescription: Rips by Triumph pays the best buyback here, 100% of market value in cash. But every recurring reward is locked until you buy a pack. Our full review.

sections.heading: The best buyback in the category, and it pays cash
body: Triumph advertises 100% of fair market value on buybacks, and independent testing reports it paying out in cash rather than site credit. Those two facts together make it the strongest set of terms of any rip site we have looked at.

The distinction matters more than the percentage. Packz also advertises 90%, which sounds close, but Packz pays that into store credit that can only buy more packs. The money never leaves. Triumph's comes out. If you only read one line about any site in this category, read the one that says what you get paid in.

Understand what 100% is measured against, though. It is 100% of Triumph's valuation of the card you pulled, not 100% of what the pack cost you. Pull a six dollar card from a forty dollar pack and the buyback pays six dollars. That is still the best deal going, but it is not a refund.

sections.heading: Now the part that will annoy you
body: Triumph runs three recurring rewards: a daily Cash Drop, a weekly Free Pack and a monthly Free Pack. Every single one of them is padlocked until you buy a pack.

Open a new account and all three sit there at 0%, with a small lock icon and the words 'Buy a pack to unlock this reward' underneath. The daily is the same, carrying a 'Buy a pack' tag where the claim button should be.

The Cash Drop also scales with spending rather than attendance. Triumph's own wording is that the more packs you buy, the bigger the drop. That is a loyalty programme, and there is nothing wrong with running one, but it is not a daily reward in the way Tilt Rips or Crown Rips mean it. Anyone arriving expecting free value from day one is going to bounce off this.
You also have to claim the Cash Drop within 23 hours or it disappears, so it wants daily attention on top of the spending.

sections.heading: What you get for the money
body: Packs run from $1 up to $1,000, and odds are displayed before you buy. That transparency is standard among the better operators here and absent from the worse ones.

After a rip you get seven days to decide whether to ship the card or sell it back, which is the most generous decision window we have measured. Crown Rips gives you three days before it sells the card out from under you. Seven is enough to actually think about it.
Identity verification is mandatory before you can withdraw or ship anything, so do it when you sign up rather than when you are waiting on money.

sections.heading: Who is behind it
body: The App Store copyright line reads Triumph TCG, LLC, based in San Francisco. Other listings credit Triumph Labs, and the Android bundle identifier points at Triumph Arcade, so the corporate naming is tangled. The company's own site resolves to Triumph Labs.
It is app-only. There is no browser version to speak of, which is worth knowing if you prefer not to install anything.

sections.heading: So is it worth it
body: If you are going to spend money ripping packs, Triumph is where the terms are best and the decision window is longest, and the cash buyback means your balance is actually yours. On that basis it is the strongest site on this list.

If you are here to farm free value without spending, it is close to useless. Everything recurring is behind a purchase, and Tilt Rips will hand you a free pack every day with no such condition. We would open both: Triumph for the terms when you do spend, Tilt Rips for the daily when you do not.

faqs.q: Does Rips by Triumph have a free daily reward?
faqs.a: It has a daily Cash Drop, but it is locked until you buy a pack, as are the weekly and monthly free pack rewards. On a new account with no purchase, all three stay padlocked at 0%.

faqs.q: Does Rips by Triumph pay out in cash or store credit?
faqs.a: Cash. Its 100% fair market value buyback has been reported paying out as withdrawable cash rather than site credit, which is the single biggest thing separating it from sites like Packz that pay in credit only.

faqs.q: How long do you have to decide on a card at Rips by Triumph?
faqs.a: Seven days to either ship it or sell it back, which is the longest decision window of any rip site we track. Crown Rips, by comparison, auto-sells anything left in the vault after three days.

faqs.q: Does the Triumph daily Cash Drop get bigger over time?
faqs.a: It gets bigger the more you spend, not the longer you play. The app states that the more packs you buy, the bigger the drop, so it rewards spending rather than daily attendance.

faqs.q: Is Rips by Triumph legit?
faqs.a: Yes. It operates as Triumph TCG, LLC out of San Francisco, publishes pack odds before purchase, and requires identity verification before any withdrawal or shipment. Reviewers consistently report the buyback paying as advertised.

eligibility.note: Triumph's own regulatory FAQ says Rips is offered throughout the United States except for Nevada. Worth separating from the longer exclusion list you may see quoted elsewhere, which covers Triumph Arcade's cash skill tournaments rather than Rips: that product also bars Arizona, Connecticut, Delaware, Louisiana, Maine, Michigan, Montana, South Dakota and Tennessee. Those do not apply here.

sections.heading: Graded cards, which makes this a different product
body: Most rip sites hand you a raw card and an opinion about what it is worth. CrownCards deals in graded cards, and that changes the maths in a way worth understanding before you compare it to anything else on this list.

A graded card carries an independent assessment of its condition, which is most of what determines its value. When a site sells you raw cards and then offers to buy them back at its own valuation, you are trusting that valuation completely. When the card is graded, there is a third party in the middle and much less room for interpretation.
If you are ripping because you actually want cards rather than a cash balance, that is a meaningful advantage and the main reason to look here.

sections.heading: The best odds disclosure we have seen here
body: CrownCards publishes more detail about pull rates than any other operator we looked at, and in a category this young that is genuinely unusual. Two of the eight sites we track publish nothing at all.

This matters because odds disclosure is the only way to sanity-check what a pack is worth. Without it you are guessing, and the operator is not. We would rather send people to a site that tells you the numbers than one with a flashier welcome offer and nothing behind it.

sections.heading: The buyback is 100%, and it pays out
body: We originally marked this down because CrownCards did not publish a buyback rate anywhere obvious. It does, in its own FAQ: you can accept an available buyback offer for 100% of fair market value, and withdrawals run through a Cash Out option on your profile once you have verified your identity, which takes a couple of minutes.

That puts CrownCards level with Crown Rips and Rips by Triumph on the single most important term in this category, and ahead of Packz, whose 90% is paid in store credit that can only ever buy more packs.

One piece of wording to hold onto. The FAQ says you can accept an available buyback offer, which implies the offer has to exist on that item rather than being guaranteed on everything you pull. We have not seen it documented when an offer would not be available, so treat 100% as the rate when a buyback is offered rather than as a promise on every card.
As always, 100% is measured against the operator's valuation of what you pulled, not against what the pack cost you. Those are different numbers on every site in this category.

sections.heading: The daily is better than it first looks
body: The seven-day cycle pays small change through the week, five cents a day at the start, which is not why anyone turns up. Day seven is a Pokemon Starter Pack, and that is.

The longer milestone track is the real draw. Hit day fourteen and you get another Starter Pack, day twenty-one upgrades to a Select Pack, and day thirty pays a Mega Pack. No purchase is needed for any of it. That makes a month of logins worth four packs and roughly thirty cents, which is a reasonable return on doing nothing.
Like every streak in this category, the value sits at the back end. Starting on day one and not missing is worth considerably more than drifting in and out.

sections.heading: A note on the name
body: CrownCards and Crown Rips are not the same company and have no connection to each other, despite both appearing on lists like this one and sharing a word. CrownCards is Crown Cards LLC, registered in Cheyenne, Wyoming, and launched in June 2026. Crown Rips is a separate operator entirely.
Some earlier write-ups elsewhere linked CrownCards to Crown Coins, the sweepstakes casino. We can find no evidence of any relationship, and we would treat claims of one with suspicion.

dailyReward.note: Pullz runs a stamp card rather than a daily drop. You tap to stamp once a day, and a full streak of seven stamps unlocks a weekly pack. The pack tier climbs as you progress through four levels, from the Fan Pack capped at $5, to Member at $7, Streak at $10 and Loyalty at $15, with the upper three locked until you work up to them. Those are ceilings on what a pack can contain rather than values. Note that the reward here is weekly, not daily, so it pays less often than it first appears.

seoTitle: Pullz Review 2026: Is It Legit? Payout Issues
metaDescription: Pullz runs a daily stamp card that unlocks a weekly pack, but recent app reviews are dominated by withdrawal complaints and the buyback has no published floor.

sections.heading: The short answer on whether Pullz is legit
body: Pullz is a real app from a real company and people do get paid by it. That is not the same as recommending it, and we do not.

The problem is concentrated in one place, and it is the worst possible place for it to be: withdrawals. A review aggregator that tracks this category found that 110 of the 169 most recent App Store reviews were one star, and that roughly 68 of the low-rated reviews from a two-month window were specifically about withdrawals that never arrived. Some users do report fast payouts, including funds landing in under a business day. The picture is not uniformly bad. It is badly split.

When reports about a site's payouts split like that, the sensible read is not that half the users are lying. It is that something inconsistent is happening, and you do not want to find out which half you are in with a balance built up.

sections.heading: The buyback term that should stop you
body: Pullz does not publish a fixed buyback percentage. The marketing says you can sell any pull back at market value with funds hitting your balance in seconds, which sounds fine.
The terms reportedly allow buyback offers at, above or below fair market value, including pricing set per individual user.

Read that again, because it is the single most unusual clause we have come across in this category. Every other site on this list commits to a number. Crown Rips says 100%. Tilt Rips says 90%. Packz says 90% and tells you it is credit. Pullz reserves the right to decide what your card is worth, and to decide it differently for you than for someone else.

There may be a benign operational reason for that wording. But a buyback with no published floor and per-user pricing is not something you can plan around, and it is not something we can tell readers is safe.

The marketing is also worth holding up against the complaints. Pullz tells you funds hit your balance in seconds and that you can withdraw whenever you like. A large share of recent one-star reviews are from people saying precisely that did not happen. We are not calling the claim false, because plenty of users do get paid quickly. But a promise of instant withdrawals carries less weight when the loudest feedback about the site concerns withdrawals that never arrived.

sections.heading: What it does well
body: Credit where it is due: Pullz shows the minimum and maximum card value in a pack before you buy it. Most of its competitors do not, and it is a genuinely useful piece of information.

The daily stamp card is also a decent mechanic. You tap once a day, and seven stamps unlock a weekly pack. The tier climbs as you progress, from the Fan Pack capped at $5 through Member at $7 and Streak at $10 to Loyalty at $15.
Be clear about the frequency, though. It is presented as a daily, and the stamping is daily, but the reward is weekly. That is a slower drip than it looks at a glance.

sections.heading: Other things to know before signing up
body: There is a reported $200 daily cap on withdrawals, so a large balance comes out slowly even when everything goes right.
Shipping is reportedly unavailable to thirteen US states. Which thirteen is not published anywhere we could find, so check your own before assuming you can get a card posted to you.
The referral link is just the App Store listing rather than a tracked URL, which means the code has to be entered inside the app during signup or it does not attach.

sections.heading: Our advice
body: If you want to try it, treat the free pack as the ceiling of your exposure. Claim it, sell it back, and withdraw immediately. Do not let a balance build, and do not deposit until you have personally watched a withdrawal clear.
There are sites in this category with published buyback floors, cash payouts and no pattern of payout complaints. Crown Rips and Rips by Triumph both qualify. We would start with those.

faqs.q: Is Pullz legit or a scam?
faqs.a: Pullz is a real app and some users report fast payouts, but recent App Store reviews are heavily weighted toward one star, with a large share specifically about withdrawals that never arrived. We would not recommend building a balance there without first watching a small withdrawal clear.

faqs.q: What is the Pullz buyback rate?
faqs.a: There is no published rate. The terms reportedly permit buyback offers at, above or below fair market value, including pricing set per individual user, which means there is no floor you can rely on.

faqs.q: Is there a withdrawal limit on Pullz?
faqs.a: A $200 daily cap has been reported, so a larger balance takes several days to come out even when withdrawals are processing normally.

faqs.q: How does the Pullz daily stamp work?
faqs.a: You tap to stamp once a day, and a full streak of seven stamps unlocks a weekly pack. The pack tier rises through four levels, from the Fan Pack capped at $5 up to the Loyalty Pack capped at $15. The stamping is daily but the reward is weekly.

faqs.q: Can Pullz ship cards to my state?
faqs.a: Possibly not. Shipping is reportedly unavailable to thirteen US states, and the list is not published anywhere we could find, so check before assuming you can have a card posted to you.

eligibility.note: Pullz's terms name no prohibited US state. They define a Prohibited Jurisdiction without listing one, and reserve the right to add or remove jurisdictions at any time and to decline shipment to certain addresses. Reports of shipping being unavailable in thirteen states come from users rather than from the terms, and we could not confirm which states those are. The contracting entity is Delta Two.

metaDescription: PrizePicks launched digital rips in October 2026, buying cards back at 100% of fair market value into a withdrawable balance. Our review of the terms and the catch.

sections.heading: The biggest name in pick'em just entered card rips
body: PrizePicks launched its digital pack product in the second half of October 2026. For a category made up almost entirely of startups less than a year old, a major established operator arriving is the most significant thing that has happened to it.

It is not alone. Underdog moved into rips just before PrizePicks did, and Fanatics and Betr are both active in the space. What began as a scattering of apps is turning into a product line that serious companies want.

Packs cover basketball, football and Pokemon, priced from $1 up to $2,500. Odds and the potential card values are shown before you open anything, which is the standard the better operators in this category already meet.

sections.heading: Why scale matters here more than usual
body: This category is lightly regulated and most of its operators are small, new, and have everything to gain from an aggressive buyback valuation and not much to lose from an unhappy customer.

PrizePicks is in a different position. It has a large existing customer base in a business where payment reliability is the entire product, and a reputation that is worth considerably more than any single disputed card valuation. That is not a guarantee of good behaviour, but the incentives point the right way, which is more than can be said for some of the apps on this list.
Its terms frame the product as ecommerce rather than gambling. That framing is the company's own, and it is the same reasoning that lets rip sites operate in states where sweepstakes casinos cannot.

sections.heading: The terms are better than we expected
body: At launch there was no published buyback percentage, which for a few days made PrizePicks impossible to judge on the one term that decides whether a rip site is worth using. That has been answered, and the answer is good.

The buyback is 100% of a card's fair market value. Proceeds go to your PrizePicks balance, where they can be spent across the company's other products or withdrawn to a bank account. That is a withdrawable balance rather than ring-fenced store credit, which puts PrizePicks level with the best terms in this category.

There is a detail here that is genuinely better than the competition. The buyback offer holds for three days and does not change during that window. On most rip sites a valuation moves with the market while you are deciding, so the number you were offered is not necessarily the number you get. A frozen offer gives you three days to think without the price drifting under you.

The catch attached to it: if you do nothing for three days, the card sells back automatically. Shipping has a tighter window still, reportedly needing to be actioned from your Locker within about 24 hours, and shipping fees apply. If you pull something you want to keep, act on the day.

sections.heading: What is still missing
body: There is no daily or recurring reward of any kind. Tilt Rips gives a free pack every single day, Crown Rips gives three a week and CrownCards pays packs at four milestones a month, all without a purchase. PrizePicks gives you nothing for turning up, which is the main reason it sits where it does on this list despite having excellent terms.

And the product is days old. There is no body of user reports about how disputes or withdrawals actually go, no sense of how valuations hold up over time, and no track record to point at. Good terms on paper are not the same as a record of honouring them, and every operator in this category looks fine in week one.
The usual advice applies with more force here than anywhere: rip something small, sell it back, withdraw it, and confirm the whole pipeline works before you treat it as somewhere to build a balance.

sections.heading: Our position for now
body: Worth watching rather than committing to. The operator is the most credible in the category by a distance, but the terms that decide whether a rip site is worth using are not published yet.

If you already use PrizePicks for pick'em, trying a small pack costs you nothing in trust you have not already extended. If you are coming to it fresh looking for free value, there is none here yet, and Tilt Rips will give you a free pack every day.

faqs.q: When did PrizePicks Packs launch?
faqs.a: Mid-to-late October 2026, with coverage dating the rollout to around 15 October and the official announcement on 21 October. It is one of the newest products in the category.

faqs.q: Does PrizePicks Packs have a daily reward?
faqs.a: Not that we have found. If free daily value is what you are after, Tilt Rips gives a free pack every day and Crown Rips gives three a week, both without a purchase.

faqs.q: What is the PrizePicks Packs buyback rate?
faqs.a: 100% of fair market value. Proceeds go to your PrizePicks balance, where they can be used across its other products or withdrawn to a bank account. The buyback offer holds for three days without changing, after which the card sells back automatically.

faqs.q: How much do PrizePicks packs cost?
faqs.a: From $1 up to $2,500, covering basketball, football and Pokemon. Odds and potential card values are displayed before you open a pack.

eligibility.note: PrizePicks states that Packs is available in all 50 states, which is unusual enough to be a genuine selling point. Note that this is the Packs product specifically: the PrizePicks pick'em product is restricted in a number of states, and the two are not the same thing. Eligibility still requires that you are legally allowed to use PrizePicks where you are.

metaDescription: Courtside is a social sportsbook with Pokemon rips built in. Packs cost coins rather than dollars, and cards cannot be shipped at all. Our full review.

sections.heading: This is a sportsbook with rips attached, not a rip site
body: Courtside is a social sportsbook first. The Pokemon rip feature sits inside it as one more thing to spend coins on, alongside the picks and the slots, and that framing explains almost everything about how it behaves.

Packs are priced in Courtside Coins rather than dollars, somewhere between 1,000 and 25,000 of them. That is a deliberate design choice and not a neutral one: pricing in a currency you bought earlier makes it considerably harder to feel what a pack actually costs. Every other site on this list prices in dollars.

sections.heading: You cannot get the card
body: This is the part that disqualifies Courtside for most people reading a card rips page. Cards cannot be shipped. There is no option to have one posted to you, no vault to store it in, and no route to physically owning anything you pull.

What you can do is convert a card into Courtside Coins, which can then be turned into real cash. So there is a path to value, and it is not a dead end. But if the appeal of ripping packs is the card at the end of it, this is the wrong app, and no other feature compensates for that.
Pack odds are not published either, which makes Courtside one of only two sites on our list offering no visibility into what you are buying.

sections.heading: What it is actually good for
body: If you already have a Courtside balance from the sportsbook side, ripping a pack is a reasonable way to use it, and the app itself is well regarded, holding about 4.7 on iOS and 4.5 on Android.
The rips also give you something to do with coins that would otherwise sit idle, and the conversion route back to cash means it is not a one-way door.
Treat it as a feature of a sportsbook you were going to use anyway rather than a reason to sign up. If card rips are what you came for, the sites built specifically for it do the job properly.

faqs.q: Can you ship cards from Courtside?
faqs.a: No. Cards cannot be shipped at all. The only option is converting a card into Courtside Coins, which can then be turned into cash. If you want the physical card, use a dedicated rip site instead.

faqs.q: How much do Courtside packs cost?
faqs.a: Between 1,000 and 25,000 Courtside Coins. Pricing in coins rather than dollars makes the real cost of a pack harder to judge than on sites that price in dollars.

faqs.q: Does Courtside publish pack odds?
faqs.a: No. It is one of only two sites on our list that offers no visibility into pull rates before you buy.

faqs.q: Is Courtside worth using for card rips?
faqs.a: Only if you already use it as a sportsbook and have coins sitting idle. As a dedicated card rip platform it is the weakest option here, mainly because you can never take delivery of a card.

eligibility.note: Courtside's terms name no prohibited US state, referring only to jurisdictions where use is prohibited without listing any. Given it runs a social sportsbook alongside the rips, confirm your own state at signup rather than relying on the absence of a list.

seoTitle: Packz Review 2026: 90% Buyback, Paid in Credit
metaDescription: Packz publishes pull rates and holds real sealed product, but its 90% buyback pays store credit rather than cash. Our review of the terms.

sections.heading: 90% sounds competitive until you read the next word
body: Packz buys cards back at 90% of fair market value. Tilt Rips offers the same rate. On a comparison table those two look interchangeable, and they are not, because Packz pays in site credit.

Credit can only ever buy more packs. It cannot be withdrawn, it cannot be spent anywhere else, and it means that money you put into Packz stays in Packz permanently, cycling through pack after pack until it runs out. Which, given packs are a negative-expectation purchase, it eventually will.
That is the whole review in one paragraph, and it is why Packz ranks where it does despite doing several things well. A rate is only worth what you can do with the proceeds.

The welcome offer is a partial exception. New accounts get a first pack of up to $100 carrying a 100% buyback rather than the standard 90%. Read the conditions on it though: the bonus funds are non-withdrawable and the whole thing expires in 48 hours.

sections.heading: The 72-hour clock on anything you do not ship
body: Cards you do not ship are sold back automatically after 72 hours. That is tighter than everything on this list except Crown Rips, and considerably tighter than the seven days Rips by Triumph allows.
Combined with the credit-only buyback, the practical effect is that a card you forget about for three days converts itself into store credit. Not cash. Credit.
Shipping is US-only, and there is no PayPal or crypto option for moving money.

sections.heading: What Packz does genuinely well
body: It publishes pull rates, which puts it ahead of Courtside and Pullz, and it reportedly holds real sealed product rather than operating purely as a numbers game. For a category where provenance is mostly taken on trust, that is worth saying.
It has also been running since September 2025, which makes it one of the longer-established operators here. Most of its competitors launched in 2026. A track record is not nothing.

sections.heading: The friction is at the cashier, not the rip
body: Opening packs on Packz is not where the problems are. The pull rates are published, the product is real, and the ripping itself works as advertised. Everything awkward about this site happens afterwards, when you try to turn a card into something you can spend.

Start with the buyback paying credit rather than cash, so the proceeds cannot leave the site. Add the 72-hour clock that converts anything unshipped into more of that credit. Add shipping that is US-only, with no PayPal and no crypto to move money by. Then add the repeated identity and selfie verification checks users report running into.

None of those is damning by itself. Together they describe a system that is easy to put money into and awkward to take value out of, and that pattern is worth recognising before you deposit rather than after.

sections.heading: Should you use it
body: Only if you are treating the whole thing as entertainment and have genuinely made peace with the money not coming back out. The pull-rate transparency and the sealed-product claim make it a more honest place to spend than some of its competitors, but credit-only buybacks make it a closed loop by design.
If what you want is a rip site where a balance can become money, Crown Rips and Rips by Triumph both pay cash and both publish their rates.

faqs.q: Does Packz pay out in cash?
faqs.a: No. The standard 90% buyback is paid as site credit, which can only be used to buy more packs. It cannot be withdrawn. That is the most important thing to understand about Packz.

faqs.q: What is the Packz welcome offer?
faqs.a: A first pack of up to $100 carrying a 100% buyback instead of the usual 90%. The bonus funds are non-withdrawable and the offer expires 48 hours after signup.

faqs.q: What is the catch with Packz?
faqs.a: The ripping works fine; the friction is all at the cashier. The buyback pays credit rather than cash, unshipped cards convert to more credit after 72 hours, shipping is US-only with no PayPal or crypto, and users report repeated identity and selfie verification checks.

faqs.q: How long do I have to ship a card from Packz?
faqs.a: 72 hours. Anything you have not shipped by then is automatically sold back, and the proceeds arrive as site credit rather than cash.

eligibility.note: Section 3.3 of the Packz terms states plainly that the service is not available in Nevada. The same section reserves the right to change eligible locations at any time and at its sole discretion, so it is worth re-checking rather than assuming.
